capability: Each note keeps its own space; compare only shared parts
title: Give each note its own card.

hook.picture: Close: the whale pours notes of every size into one flat tray. Each one squashes into the same flat card. A wrong link between two cards hides among the rest.
hook.words: I put every note in one box.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: Everything sits in one space, so nothing ever looks wrong.
problem_in_viewer_words.who: a researcher reviewing a knowledge graph

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: a vast flat sheet of identical cards. Three times, every 2 beats, then 1, then half, a wrong link drops in and vanishes into the sameness.
why_it_keeps_happening.words: When all notes look alike, errors hide.

stakes.body: A wrong link survives review, and every answer built on it inherits the error.

solution_hint: Let each note keep its own shape.

metaphor.body: Notes are cards of different heights instead of one flat pile. Neighbours are compared only on the part they share, so a wrong link shows up as a visible gap.

steps.picture: The cards lift out of the tray and each grows to its own height: small notes short, rich notes tall. The line threads through their tops.
steps.words: Let each note keep its own shape.
steps.sound: Each card sounds its own pitch, low to high.

steps.picture: Between two neighbours a dashed join appears. A small arrow carries only the shared part of each card onto it. Matching parts tick teal.
steps.words: Compare only the part two notes share.
steps.sound: Unison pairs on each teal join.

steps.picture: Push-in: the once hidden wrong link sits on a join whose two arrows miss each other. The gap glows English Red, and its width shows how far apart they are.
steps.words: The wrong link cannot hide now.
steps.sound: The pair beats, wider gap, faster beat.

steps.picture: A label slides onto one tall card: stalk. The whale rings the red gap; it stays lit for review.
steps.words: What one note holds: its stalk.
steps.sound: Ring tone, then the beating pair holds.

real_case.claim: Three independent libraries (Rust, Python, Haskell) gave identical results and edge discord on the 215-node FRONTIER sheaf.

honest_limit.picture: Push to one join: one card speaks in miles, its neighbour in kilometres. The plain copy arrow cannot translate, so the join glows red though both cards are right.
honest_limit.words: Same fact, two units. Marked wrong.

not_this.body: Plain copy maps cannot translate meaning.

ending_pattern.body: The same tray, but the cards now stand at their own heights and the once hidden wrong link glows red in plain view as the whale circles it.
ending_pattern.callback: The link that hid in the flat pile in bar 1 stands out red in the same framing.

end_belief.body: Let notes differ. Compare them where they meet.

sound.signature: A pitch per card height; shared parts ring in unison across a join.
sound.problem_motif: All cards on one flat pitch, smeared together, with one sour beat buried inside.

score_self.reason: The flat-pile vs own-height picture is strong. The limit (no translation between units) is honest and caution-backed but may be too subtle at phone size. The case card hides H⁰ correctly.
